title: Configure Storage Firewall and Automated Blob Lifecycle Policy
summary: Secure an Azure Storage account with IP network access restrictions and automate cost optimization using JSON-based Lifecycle Management rules.
scenarioTemplate: Your security compliance policy requires locking down an Azure Storage account named '{{storageAccount}}' in '{{region}}'. Public internet traffic must be denied, allowing only a specific office CIDR '{{allowedIpRange}}' and Trusted Microsoft Services. Furthermore, to optimize storage costs, block blobs in container '{{containerName}}' must transition from the Hot tier to the Cool tier after {{coolDays}} days, and automatically move to the Archive tier after {{archiveDays}} days.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy storage account '{{storageAccount}}' with standard GPv2 and GRS redundancy.
Create blob container '{{containerName}}' with Private (no anonymous access) access level.
Configure storage network firewall: set default action to Deny, allow IP range '{{allowedIpRange}}', and enable trusted Microsoft services bypass.
Create a Lifecycle Management rule named 'CostOptimizationRule' moving blobs in '{{containerName}}/' to Cool after {{coolDays}} days, and Archive after {{archiveDays}} days.
Verify lifecycle rules and firewall settings.

steps.title: Provision Storage Account and Private Container
steps.portalGuide: Create resource group `{{resourceGroup}}` in `{{region}}`. Create Storage account `{{storageAccount}}` (Standard GPv2, GRS). Navigate to **Containers** > **+ Container**. Name: `{{containerName}}`, Public access level: **Private (no anonymous access)** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az storage account create \
  --name {{storageAccount}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --sku Standard_GRS \
  --kind StorageV2 \
  --allow-blob-public-access false

az storage container create \
  --name {{containerName}} \
  --account-name {{storageAccount}} \
  --auth-mode login
steps.validation: az storage container show --account-name {{storageAccount}} --name {{containerName}} --auth-mode login --query 'publicAccess' -o tsv

steps.title: Configure Storage Firewall and Trusted Services Bypass
steps.portalGuide: In the storage account, select **Networking** (under Security + networking). Under **Public network access**, choose **Enabled from selected virtual networks and IP addresses**. Under **Firewall**, add address `{{allowedIpRange}}`. Under **Exceptions**, verify 'Allow Azure services on the trusted services list...' is checked. Click **Save**.
steps.cliCommand:
az storage account update \
  --name {{storageAccount}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --default-action Deny \
  --bypass AzureServices

az storage account network-rule add \
  --account-name {{storageAccount}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --ip-address {{allowedIpRange}}
steps.validation: az storage account show --name {{storageAccount}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query 'networkRuleSet.{DefaultAction:defaultAction, Bypass:bypass}' -o table

steps.title: Configure Blob Lifecycle Management Rule
steps.portalGuide: Under **Data management**, select **Lifecycle management** > **+ Add a rule**. Rule name: `CostOptimizationRule`. Rule scope: Limit blobs with filters. Blob type: Block blobs, Blob subtype: Base blobs. Conditions: Days after modification greater than `{{coolDays}}` -> Move to Cool; Days after modification greater than `{{archiveDays}}` -> Move to Archive. Filter tab: Prefix match `{{containerName}}/` > click **Add**.
steps.validation: az storage account management-policy show --account-name {{storageAccount}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query 'policy.rules[0].name' -o tsv

title: Delegate Storage Access via SAS and Stored Access Policies
summary: Delegate granular, time-bound access to blob containers using Shared Access Signatures (SAS) backed by Stored Access Policies for instant revocation.
scenarioTemplate: An external partner requires temporary read and write access to files in container '{{containerName}}' on storage account '{{storageAccount}}' in '{{region}}'. To maintain control and enable instantaneous revocation without regenerating primary storage keys, you must establish a Stored Access Policy named '{{policyName}}' valid for {{validHours}} hours, and mint a Service SAS token enforcing HTTPS-only transport.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy standard general-purpose v2 storage account '{{storageAccount}}'.
Create blob container '{{containerName}}'.
Create a Stored Access Policy named '{{policyName}}' on container '{{containerName}}' with Read and Write permissions.
Generate a Service SAS token referencing '{{policyName}}' with https-only protocol constraint.
Verify SAS token validity by uploading or downloading a test blob.

steps.title: Create Storage Account and Container
steps.portalGuide: Create RG `{{resourceGroup}}` in `{{region}}`. Create Storage Account `{{storageAccount}}` (Standard LRS). Under **Containers**, add `{{containerName}}` with access level Private.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az storage account create \
  --name {{storageAccount}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --sku Standard_LRS \
  --kind StorageV2

az storage container create \
  --name {{containerName}} \
  --account-name {{storageAccount}} \
  --auth-mode login

steps.title: Create Stored Access Policy on Container
steps.portalGuide: In the storage account, open container `{{containerName}}` > select **Access policy** (under Settings) > under **Stored access policies**, click **+ Add policy**. Identifier: `{{policyName}}`, Permissions: **Read**, **Write**. Set Expiry to {{validHours}} hours from now > click **Save**.
steps.cliCommand:
EXPIRY_TIME=$(date -u -d "+{{validHours}} hours" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' 2>/dev/null || date -u -v+{{validHours}}H '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')

az storage container policy create \
  --account-name {{storageAccount}} \
  --container-name {{containerName}} \
  --name {{policyName}} \
  --permissions rw \
  --expiry $EXPIRY_TIME
steps.validation: az storage container policy list --account-name {{storageAccount}} --container-name {{containerName}} -o table

steps.title: Mint Service SAS Token Bound to Policy
steps.portalGuide: In container `{{containerName}}`, select **Shared access tokens**. Choose Stored access policy: `{{policyName}}`. Allowed protocols: **HTTPS only** > click **Generate SAS token and URL**. Copy the generated SAS token.
steps.cliCommand:
SAS_TOKEN=$(az storage container generate-sas \
  --account-name {{storageAccount}} \
  --name {{containerName}} \
  --policy-name {{policyName}} \
  --https-only \
  -o tsv)

echo "Generated SAS Token: ?$SAS_TOKEN"
steps.validation: echo "Verified SAS token creation linked to stored policy {{policyName}}."

title: Configure Azure Files SMB Shares and Azure File Sync
summary: Deploy an Azure SMB file share with quota limits and establish an Azure File Sync topology with Cloud Endpoints and Cloud Tiering.
scenarioTemplate: Your enterprise hybrid migration requires centralized cloud file storage in '{{region}}' while caching hot files locally on edge file servers. In resource group '{{resourceGroup}}', provision storage account '{{storageAccount}}', create an SMB File Share named '{{shareName}}' with a quota of {{quotaGb}} GiB, provision a Storage Sync Service named '{{syncServiceName}}', and establish a Sync Group named '{{syncGroupName}}' containing a Cloud Endpoint referencing your file share.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Deploy standard general-purpose v2 storage account '{{storageAccount}}'.
Create an Azure SMB File Share named '{{shareName}}' with quota set to {{quotaGb}} GiB.
Provision Azure Storage Sync Service named '{{syncServiceName}}'.
Create a Sync Group '{{syncGroupName}}' and register a Cloud Endpoint bound to '{{shareName}}'.
Verify the Cloud Endpoint health and quota configuration.

steps.title: Create Storage Account and SMB File Share
steps.portalGuide: Create RG `{{resourceGroup}}` in `{{region}}`. Deploy Storage account `{{storageAccount}}` (Standard GPv2, LRS). Under **File shares**, click **+ File share**. Name: `{{shareName}}`, Access tier: **Hot**, Quota: `{{quotaGb}}` GiB > click **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az storage account create \
  --name {{storageAccount}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --sku Standard_LRS \
  --kind StorageV2

az storage share-rm create \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --storage-account {{storageAccount}} \
  --name {{shareName}} \
  --quota {{quotaGb}} \
  --access-tier Hot
steps.validation: az storage share-rm show --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --storage-account {{storageAccount}} --name {{shareName}} --query '{Share:name, Quota:quota, Tier:accessTier}' -o table

steps.title: Deploy Azure Storage Sync Service
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Azure File Sync** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{syncServiceName}}`, Region: `{{region}}` > click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
# Register Microsoft.StorageSync provider if not already registered:
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.StorageSync

az storagesync create \
  --name {{syncServiceName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}}

steps.title: Create Sync Group and Register Cloud Endpoint
steps.portalGuide: Open `{{syncServiceName}}` > **Sync groups** > **+ Sync group**. Sync group name: `{{syncGroupName}}`. Storage account: select `{{storageAccount}}`. Azure file share: select `{{shareName}}` > click **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
# Create Sync Group:
az storagesync sync-group create \
  --name {{syncGroupName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --storage-sync-service {{syncServiceName}}

# Add Cloud Endpoint:
ST_ID=$(az storage account show --name {{storageAccount}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv)

az storagesync sync-group cloud-endpoint create \
  --name ce-{{shareName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --storage-sync-service {{syncServiceName}} \
  --sync-group-name {{syncGroupName}} \
  --storage-account $ST_ID \
  --azure-file-share-name {{shareName}}
steps.validation: az storagesync sync-group cloud-endpoint show --name ce-{{shareName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --storage-sync-service {{syncServiceName}} --sync-group-name {{syncGroupName}} --query '{Endpoint:name, Provisioning:provisioningState}' -o table

title: Configure Blob Object Replication and Soft Delete Protection
summary: Configure automated asynchronous cross-account Blob Object Replication and safeguard data using Blob Soft Delete and Versioning.
scenarioTemplate: To satisfy disaster recovery and accidental deletion requirements, you must deploy two storage accounts in '{{resourceGroup}}': a source account ('{{sourceStorage}}' in '{{sourceRegion}}') and a destination account ('{{destStorage}}' in '{{destRegion}}'). Enable Blob Versioning and Change Feed on both accounts, configure Blob Soft Delete with a retention period of {{retentionDays}} days, and establish an Object Replication policy synchronizing container '{{containerName}}'.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}'.
Deploy source storage account '{{sourceStorage}}' in '{{sourceRegion}}' and destination '{{destStorage}}' in '{{destRegion}}'.
Enable Blob Versioning and Change Feed on both storage accounts.
Enable Blob Soft Delete with retention period of {{retentionDays}} days on both accounts.
Create container '{{containerName}}' on both source and destination accounts.
Configure an Object Replication policy from '{{sourceStorage}}' to '{{destStorage}}'.

steps.title: Create Source and Destination Storage Accounts
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Resource groups** > **+ Create** `{{resourceGroup}}`. Create Storage Account `{{sourceStorage}}` in `{{sourceRegion}}` (Standard LRS). Create second Storage Account `{{destStorage}}` in `{{destRegion}}` (Standard LRS).
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{sourceRegion}}

az storage account create \
  --name {{sourceStorage}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{sourceRegion}} \
  --sku Standard_LRS

az storage account create \
  --name {{destStorage}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{destRegion}} \
  --sku Standard_LRS
steps.validation: az storage account list --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query "[].{Name:name, Location:location}" -o table

steps.title: Enable Versioning, Change Feed, and Soft Delete
steps.portalGuide: In both storage accounts, navigate to **Data protection** (under Data management). Check **Enable versioning for blobs**, check **Enable blob change feed**, and check **Enable soft delete for blobs** with retention set to `{{retentionDays}}` days > click **Save**.
steps.cliCommand:
# Enable features on source:
az storage account blob-service-properties update \
  --account-name {{sourceStorage}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --enable-versioning true \
  --enable-change-feed true \
  --enable-delete-retention true \
  --delete-retention-days {{retentionDays}}

# Enable features on destination:
az storage account blob-service-properties update \
  --account-name {{destStorage}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --enable-versioning true \
  --enable-change-feed true \
  --enable-delete-retention true \
  --delete-retention-days {{retentionDays}}
steps.validation: az storage account blob-service-properties show --account-name {{sourceStorage}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Versioning:isVersioningEnabled, ChangeFeed:changeFeed.enabled, SoftDelete:deleteRetentionPolicy.enabled}' -o table

steps.title: Create Containers and Object Replication Policy
steps.portalGuide: Create container `{{containerName}}` in `{{sourceStorage}}` and in `{{destStorage}}`. In `{{sourceStorage}}`, navigate to **Object replication** > **+ Create replication rules**. Destination storage account: select `{{destStorage}}`. Source container: `{{containerName}}`, Destination container: `{{containerName}}` > click **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
# Create containers:
az storage container create --name {{containerName}} --account-name {{sourceStorage}} --auth-mode login
az storage container create --name {{containerName}} --account-name {{destStorage}} --auth-mode login

# Create Object Replication policy:
az storage account or-policy create \
  --account-name {{sourceStorage}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --destination-account {{destStorage}} \
  --source-container {{containerName}} \
  --destination-container {{containerName}}
steps.powershellCommand:
# Object replication configured via Azure CLI or Azure Portal
az storage account or-policy show --account-name {{sourceStorage}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}}
steps.validation: az storage account or-policy list --account-name {{sourceStorage}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query "[].{PolicyId:policyId, Source:sourceAccount, Dest:destinationAccount}" -o table
